findings.title: The brownfield write contract has never blocked anything, on any adapter
findings.summary: The hook runs, decides correctly, logs the denial, and lets the write through.
findings.mechanism: deny() calls process.exit(1) at line 158. Claude Code PreToolUse treats exit 2 as the blocking error and every other non-zero code as a non-blocking error, so the tool call proceeds. The only exit codes in the file are 0, 1, 0. It never emits the alternative hookSpecificOutput / permissionDecision JSON protocol either (grep -c for both returns 0).
findings.decision_logic_evidence: Fed synthetic PreToolUse payloads the checker ALLOWs all three allowlisted paths and correctly DENYs apps/web/src/components/kanban-board/** (off-limits pattern) and the unlisted apps/web/src/components/public-project/list-view.tsx (absent from allowlist).
findings.live_proof: A Write was issued to apps/web/src/components/kanban-board/__mmo_gate_probe.tmp, a path matching an off-limits pattern. The write SUCCEEDED. The file was deleted immediately; git status on kanban-board/ is clean.

three_run_progression.reported: unprovable on this adapter - the worker writes through its own process so the Write|Edit matcher never fires
three_run_progression.status_now: still true, but now the lesser problem
the matcher does fire here and the gate still cannot refuse

findings.progression_note: Stated as a progression because each run saw only part of it, and that is why it took three runs to see. claude-cli never writes files at all - the adapter spawns `claude -p --output-format json` with no --allowedTools and returns file_content, so the orchestrator performs every write via Write/Edit. That is the best case for the hook, and it is still advisory. Of the three claimed enforcement layers only two were ever live: orchestrator discipline (1) and the allowlist check run over packets.json before dispatch (2). Layer 3, described as the layer you cannot talk your way past, is a warning.
findings.corollary: Fed .sdlc/runs/<run-id>/security_review.md the checker DENYs it: .sdlc/** is off-limits and no carve-out exists for the run own output directory, contrary to the orchestrator contract which states paths under .sdlc/runs/<run-id>/ are auto-allowlisted. Had the gate ever enforced, every brownfield run would have failed on its own first artifact write at Gate 1. A safety gate that would break the product the moment it started working has clearly never been exercised in anger.
fix: 1. deny() must process.exit(2), or emit hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny".
2. Add a run-directory carve-out so .sdlc/runs/<run-id>/** is allowed before .sdlc/** is tested.

3. ORDER MATTERS: shipping (1) without (2) converts a silent no-op into a run that cannot start. Anyone reading this finding will reach for the one-character exit-code fix; applied alone it breaks every brownfield run at Gate 1 on its own first artifact write.
findings.fix_order_warning: exit(2) without the carve-out converts a silent no-op into a run that cannot start.

findings.title: The character-count estimator understates premium-tier cost, with a diagnosed cause
findings.mechanism: Per-turn context re-send, which a chars/3.8 estimate on the visible prompt cannot see. Run 3 measured 493995 cached input tokens against 136550 uncached - a 3.6x ratio. That turns run 1 three upward corrections from an anecdote into a diagnosed cause.
findings.totals_caveat: Run 3 measured $2.58435 against run 1 reported $0.9731 estimated (2.66x). This does NOT mean run 1 really cost $2.58. The runs differ in phase count and packet shape, and run 1 dispatched three codegen packets to Flash at mechanical-tier rates. The honest comparison is the per-phase ratios, not the totals.
findings.only_measurable_here: Run 3 is the only run in the set that can produce this comparison: same model and same adapter as run 1 premium tier, but auth_mode vendor, so the CLI returns real total_cost_usd.

findings.title: Review phases were 43% of run cost on a 22-line component
findings.hypothesis: Suggests the premium tier earns its keep on judgment about LARGE changes and is poor value reviewing small mechanical ones - an argument for a policy that routes review by DIFF SIZE rather than by phase name.
findings.confidence: HYPOTHESIS THIS RUN CANNOT CONFIRM. n=1, on a single small refactor. Stated as an observation to be tested, not a conclusion.

findings.title: provenance.json schema field is files_touched, not files - documentation problem
findings.detail: An orchestrator inspection script read p.files and reported 0 files recorded, a false alarm; the record was complete and correct all along (3 files with sha_before, sha_after, tracked_in_git, packet_id). Run 2 hit this identically. Two orchestrators making the same wrong assumption about the same schema is a documentation problem in the provenance contract, not two independent slips.
findings.fix: Name the field explicitly in the provenance contract docs and in the revert readers schema reference.
